canonical.title: Accessible toasts in React (2026): what's actually required, and which libraries deliver

parent.title: React toast notifications in 2026: the landscape, the a11y bill, and the server boundary

siblings.title: React toast libraries in 2026: Sonner, react-toastify, react-hot-toast, notistack and the design-system natives
siblings.summary: Sonner is the 2026 default (41M weekly installs, shadcn's toast); react-toastify is the actively-released power option; react-hot-toast is the 4.7 kB minimalist; notistack is legacy.

siblings.title: Toasts in the Next.js App Router: firing client state from the server
siblings.summary: No toast library ships a server entrypoint — the queue always lives in client memory, so an RSC app must serialize server-origin toasts through an action return value or a cookie; redirect() forecloses the first option.

siblings.title: Headless toast primitives vs batteries-included: when rolling your own pays
siblings.summary: Base UI Toast is the only primitive that is both stable and feature-complete in 2026; adopt Sonner unless multi-framework, deep theming, or anchored/custom-queue needs force a primitive.

siblings.title: Migrating off legacy toasts: toastr and react-toastify → Sonner
siblings.summary: toastr is dead (last commit 2018, needs jQuery) — migrate. react-toastify is alive (v11.1.0, Apr 2026) — don't churn a working integration.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 — Understanding SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable
sources.claim: SC 2.2.1 requires content-set time limits to be turn-off-able, adjustable 10x, or extendable with a 20s warning; a timer needs no adjustment if a non-timed alternative to the information exists.

sources.title: w3c/wcag#976 — does a disappearing toast represent a timeout?
sources.claim: Whether SC 2.2.1 applies to auto-dismissing toasts is an open W3C question raised by Patrick Lauke and still unresolved.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 — Understanding SC 2.2.3 No Timing
sources.claim: SC 2.2.3 No Timing is Level AAA and requires timing not be an essential part of the activity.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 — Understanding SC 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.claim: SC 4.1.3 (Level AA) requires status messages to be programmatically determinable and announced without receiving focus.

sources.title: ARIA APG — Alert Pattern
sources.claim: The ARIA APG alert pattern has no keyboard interaction, must not move focus, and warns that auto-disappearing alerts can fail WCAG SC 2.2.3.

sources.title: ARIA APG — Alert Example
sources.claim: The APG's own alert example pre-renders an empty alert element and injects the message text into it.

sources.title: MDN — ARIA: alert role
sources.claim: MDN states that dynamically adding an already-populated role=alert element generally produces no announcement, and that role=status should be used for non-urgent messages.

sources.title: Sara Soueidan — Accessible notifications with ARIA live regions, part 1
sources.claim: role=alert implies aria-live=assertive + aria-atomic=true, role=status implies polite; live region containers must be in the DOM before they are populated.

sources.title: Sara Soueidan — Accessible notifications with ARIA live regions, part 2
sources.claim: Assertive announcements may clear queued polite messages; multiple DOM insertions cause double announcements; aria-live is advisory only.

sources.title: Scott O'Hara — A toast to a11y toasts
sources.claim: A toast is a status message and belongs in role=status; virtual-cursor reading fires no focus event so focus-pause never helps SR users; toast actions must be duplicated in the primary document.

sources.title: Adrian Roselli — Defining toast messages
sources.claim: Lists the WCAG SCs toasts typically fail, argues live regions cannot carry interactive children, and notes GitHub removed toasts from its design system in late 2025 over accessibility issues.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 — Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
sources.claim: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (AA) requires that a focused control not be entirely obscured by author-created content, which toast stacks can violate.

sources.title: Sandro Roth — Building a React toast component (Aug 2025)
sources.claim: Teardown of Radix/React Aria/MUI/PrimeReact toast internals: NVDA does not announce a role=status element added already populated; Radix uses focus-proxy sentinels and a delayed re-render; React Aria uses F6/Shift+F6 landmark navigation.

sources.title: radix-ui/primitives#3634 — toast not announced (aria-live="off")
sources.claim: Open July 2025 issue: Radix Toast v1.2.14 renders aria-live="off" on the role=status element, so toasts are not announced; reproduced in the official docs demo across Chrome, Safari and Firefox.

sources.title: radix-ui/primitives — toast.tsx
sources.claim: Radix Toast source: role=status always, aria-live switched assertive/polite by type; announce text rendered on the next frame for NVDA; default hotkey F8; viewport is role=region labelled with the hotkey.

sources.title: Radix Primitives — Toast
sources.claim: Radix Toast docs: F8 focuses the viewport, foreground toasts announced immediately, background at next opportunity; pauses closing on hover, focus and window blur.

sources.title: emilkowalski/sonner#306 — live region must always be present
sources.claim: Sonner previously rendered role=status only while a toast existed, so Windows Narrator and older iOS VoiceOver never announced toasts; closed via PR #436.

sources.title: emilkowalski/sonner — src/index.tsx
sources.claim: Sonner source: persistent section with aria-live=polite and no assertive/alert anywhere; TOAST_LIFETIME 4000ms; hotkey altKey+KeyT; container tabIndex -1, toasts tabIndex 0; pauses when expanded, interacting or document hidden.

sources.title: emilkowalski/sonner — src/styles.css
sources.claim: Sonner ships a prefers-reduced-motion guard that disables all toast transitions and animations.

sources.title: The Front Kit — shadcn/ui accessibility audit (Apr 2026)
sources.claim: April 2026 shadcn/ui audit (WCAG 2.2 AA; NVDA + VoiceOver) flags Sonner's 4-second default auto-dismiss as a SC 2.2.1 failure and recommends 8s plus a close button.

sources.title: react-toastify — Accessibility docs
sources.claim: react-toastify defaults every toast to ARIA role alert, exposes an ariaLabel prop, and focuses the first toast on Alt+T.

sources.title: fkhadra/react-toastify#1122 — toasts silent in Firefox+Orca
sources.claim: Open issue: react-toastify toasts with role=alert are not announced in Firefox+Orca because the live region is created when the toast pops.

sources.title: react-toastify — releases
sources.claim: react-toastify v11 (16 Dec 2024) added the ariaLabel prop and the Alt+T hotkey that focuses the first visible notification.

sources.title: react-toastify — ToastContainer.tsx
sources.claim: react-toastify's persistent container carries aria-live=polite; defaults are role 'alert', aria-label 'Notifications Alt+T', hotKeys altKey+KeyT focusing the first [tabIndex=0] toast.

sources.title: timolins/react-hot-toast#336 — incoherent ARIA API
sources.claim: Open issue (Jan 2024) asking react-hot-toast to fix its ARIA API: role=alert plus aria-live=assertive is redundant, and aria-live should be omitted when the role is alert.

sources.title: react-hot-toast — src/core/toast.ts
sources.claim: react-hot-toast spreads ariaProps onto the Message element that mounts already containing its text; the Toaster renders plain divs with only onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave pause handlers and no hotkey or tabIndex.

sources.title: react-hot-toast — src/core/store.ts
sources.claim: react-hot-toast default durations: blank 4000ms, error 4000ms, custom 4000ms, loading Infinity.

sources.title: notistack — MaterialDesignContent.tsx
sources.claim: notistack sets role="alert" directly on the snackbar content element, which mounts already populated, for every variant including success and info; no persistent live region, no landmark, no hotkey.

sources.title: React Aria — Toast
sources.claim: React Aria Toast: toast regions are landmarks navigable with F6 / Shift+F6, focus is restored when the last toast closes, and auto-dismiss is discouraged for critical info with a 5s minimum.

sources.title: Base UI — Toast
sources.claim: Base UI Toast: F6 jumps into the toast viewport landmark, priority low/high maps to polite/urgent announcement, default timeout 5000ms with 0 disabling auto-dismiss, default limit 3.

sources.title: Base UI — ToastViewport.tsx
sources.claim: Base UI's toast viewport carries aria-live=polite / aria-atomic=false and renders a separate role="alert" region for high-priority toasts; a global F6 keydown force-focuses the viewport.

sources.title: Base UI — ToastRoot.tsx
sources.claim: Base UI renders each toast root as a non-modal dialog, or alertdialog when priority is high, so interactive children remain reachable.
